To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamics of commitments is a special case of a more general dynamics, that of agenda-based planning, and that the statics of commitments is a more general case of that of agenda-based plans.

(i) an agent's goals are the unfulfilled wishes that it knows to have practical possibilities of implementation, (ii) an agent commits itself to those actions that it knows lead to fulfillment of some known goal, and (iii) an agent is committed, i.e., obliged to execute, those actions that it has committed itself to, but no longer knows to lead to a goal, and that it is not able to undo its commitment to.
the statics and dynamics of commitments are determined by the agent's wishes, goals and practical possibilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a logical approach to the dynamics of commitments.
a logical approach to the dynamics of commitments, which are the driving forces of an agent's actions.
the formalisation of the interplay between an agent's wishes on the one hand and its goals, commitments, and actions on the other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we provide a formalisation of the dynamics of commitments, which is based on a logical theory for the statics of motivational attitudes.

our framework provides a logical approach to the dynamics of commitments that, while being conceptually simple and intuitively clear, is sufficiently general to capture all the relevant aspects of the problem at hand.

we have presented a logical framework that allows us to model the static and dynamic aspects of the motivational attitudes of agents, and that is able to deal with complex actions and their interaction with commitments in a satisfactory way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a formalisation of the statics and dynamics of motivational attitudes in a framework which allows for a compositional treatment of actions, i.e., a formalisation that is able to cope with composite actions.
we have provided a logical approach to the dynamics of commitments, and that we have done so by means of a formalisation of the statics of motivational attitudes.
we provide an agent-oriented semantics for the notion of commitment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the formalisation of the statics and dynamics of commitments is possible in a framework that is based on the logical formalisation of actions, and that is therefore suitable for reasoning about actions, as well.

we provide a formalisation of the dynamics of motivational attitudes that is both simple and intuitive, and is based on the well-known and studied framework of Propositional Dynamic logic, thus providing a solid logical basis for our approach.
